easy.def: A big open piece of land.
examples: Cows are in the field.
We play in the field.
There is a field of flowers.

more.def: A large, open piece of land, often used for growing crops or playing sports.
examples: Cows grazed in the green field.
A field of sunflowers stretched to the hills.
The soccer team practiced on the field.

related.def: The middle part of a sports field.

examples: The tiger looks fierce.
A fierce dog barked at us.
The storm was fierce.

more.def: Wild, strong, and ready to attack; or very strong and powerful.
examples: A fierce wind bent the trees almost to the ground.
The fierce lion roared to protect her cubs.
The two teams were in a fierce battle for first place.
They had a fight.
The fight was about a toy.
We made up after the fight.

more.def: An angry argument or struggle between people or groups.
examples: The brothers had a fight about whose turn it was.
They made up after their fight and shook hands.
A fight between the two dogs ended when I called them.

easy.def: To work hard against something bad.
examples: Firefighters fight fires.
Doctors fight sickness.
We fight to win.

more.def: To try hard to stop or defeat something bad.
examples: Firefighters fought the blaze all through the night.
Doctors work hard to fight disease.
The village worked together to fight the flood.
The figure is ten.
Draw a figure.
I see a figure.

more.def: A number or amount, or the shape of a person or object.
examples: The figure on the chart showed that sales had grown.
A tall figure stood at the end of the hall.
The artist drew a figure of a dancer.
I figure it out.
Can you figure it out?
She figured out the puzzle.

more.def: To work out the answer by thinking.
examples: I figured out the riddle after thinking for a while.
Can you figure out how much money we need?
He figured that the bus would be late.

easy.def: A folder or box for papers.
examples: Put the paper in the file.
The teacher has a file.
There is a file of papers.

more.def: A folder or case used to keep papers in order.
examples: The teacher keeps each student's work in a file.
Mom put the bills in a file.
A file cabinet holds many folders.

easy.def: Work that is saved on a computer.
examples: I saved my file.
The file is big.
Open the file.

more.def: A collection of information or work that is stored on a computer.
examples: I saved my story in a computer file.
The photo file is too large to send.
She opened the file and began to type.
Fill the cup.
I filled the tub.
Fill the bucket.

more.def: To put in so much that there is no more room.
examples: Fill the glass with milk.
Dad filled the tank with gas.
She filled the basket with apples.

easy.def: To be in every part of a place.
examples: Music fills the room.
Light filled the house.
Water filled the hole.

more.def: To take up all the space in a place.
examples: Laughter filled the room.
The smell of bread filled the kitchen.
Sunlight filled the room.
We watched a film.
The film was funny.
It is a film about animals.

more.def: A story told in moving pictures, shown on a screen; a movie.
examples: We saw a film about penguins at the museum.
The film lasted nearly two hours.
She wrote a film about a talking tree.
They film a show.
Dad filmed the parade.
We filmed the dog.

more.def: To record moving pictures with a camera.
examples: Dad filmed the school play.
Scientists film the bees in the hive.
She filmed her dog doing tricks.
This is the final page.
It is the final day of school.
It was the final game.

more.def: Coming at the end; last.
examples: The final page of the book has a surprise.
The team won the final game of the season.
Friday is the final day of school.

easy.def: The last game of a contest.
examples: Our team is in the final.
She won the final.
The final starts at noon.

more.def: The last and deciding game or contest of a series.
examples: Our team played in the final on Saturday.
She won the final in two sets.
Thousands of people watched the final.

easy.def: To see or get something that was lost.
examples: I find my shoe.
She found a coin.
Can you find the cat?

more.def: To discover something, or to get something back that was lost.
examples: We found a bird's nest in the tall grass.
I could not find my glasses anywhere in the house.
The explorers found a hidden cave behind the waterfall.
I feel fine.
The weather is fine.
That is a fine idea.

more.def: Very good, or healthy and well enough.
examples: It was a fine day for a picnic by the lake.
I fell off my bike, but I am fine.
The artist did a fine job on the painting.
The thread is fine.
She has fine hair.
The sand is fine.

more.def: Very thin, small, or delicate.
examples: The spider spun a fine web between the two branches.
The beach had fine white sand that felt soft under our feet.
He drew the lines with a fine pen.

easy.def: One of the parts at the end of your hand.
examples: I have five fingers.
She pointed her finger.
He pricked his finger.

more.def: One of the long parts at the end of your hand, which you use to hold things.
examples: She pointed her finger at the map.
A pianist moves her fingers quickly.
He wore a ring on his finger.

easy.def: To come to the end of something.
examples: I finish my homework first.
She finished her lunch.
Let me finish my story.

more.def: To reach the end of something you were doing, so that nothing is left to do.
examples: Please finish your breakfast before you get dressed.
The runners finished the race in under ten minutes.
He finished painting the fence just before the rain came.

easy.def: The end of a race or a story.
examples: It was a close finish.
The book has a happy finish.
The runners raced to the finish.

more.def: The end part of something, such as a race or a story.
examples: The two swimmers touched the wall together at a very close finish.
The movie had an exciting finish that made everyone cheer.
The cyclists sprinted toward the finish.

easy.def: Flames that give heat and light.
examples: The fire is hot.
We sat by the fire.
Fire needs air.

more.def: The heat, light, and flames made when something burns.
examples: We roasted marshmallows over the campfire.
The firefighters put out the fire at the old barn.
Fire needs air to keep burning.
The mattress is firm.
The ground is firm.
A firm apple.

more.def: Hard or solid, not soft.
examples: A firm mattress is good for your back.
The ground was firm after the freeze.
Choose a firm tomato.
He gave a firm handshake.
She held on with a firm grip.
The firm rule.

more.def: Strong, steady and not easily changed.
examples: The coach gave a firm handshake.
She held the rope with a firm grip.
The teacher gave a firm rule about running.
I was the first in line.
This is my first day.
She won first prize.

more.def: Coming before all others in time, order, or importance.
examples: The first snow of the year fell last night.
Read the first chapter before the next class.
Who was the first person to fly an airplane?
Wash your hands first.
I will go first.
First, mix the eggs.

more.def: Before anything else, or at the very start.
examples: First, crack the eggs into a bowl.
She arrived first and saved us all a seat.
We first met when I was six.

easy.def: An animal that lives in water and swims with fins.
examples: A fish swims.
We saw a fish.
The fish has scales.

more.def: An animal with fins and gills that lives in water.
examples: A goldfish swam in the bowl.
Sharks are large fish with sharp teeth.
The fish hid among the rocks.

easy.def: To try to catch food from the water.
examples: We fish in the lake.
Dad fished all day.
I like to fish.

more.def: To try to catch animals from a river, lake or sea with a hook or net.
examples: We fish in the river on Saturdays.
He fished all morning but caught nothing.
Pelicans fish by diving into the sea.
The shoe fits.
The key fits the lock.
Does the hat fit?

more.def: To be the right size or shape for something.
examples: The new shoes fit well.
This key does not fit the lock.
Will all of the books fit in the bag?
He runs to stay fit.
A fit dog can run far.
She is fit.

more.def: In good health, especially from exercise.
examples: He runs every day to stay fit.
The fit athletes ran a long race.
She keeps fit by swimming.
I have five fingers.
Five plus one is six.
She is five years old.

more.def: The number 5, which is one more than four.
examples: A starfish usually has five arms.
We counted five ducks on the pond.
The bell rings at five minutes to three.
Dad will fix my bike.
She fixed the toy.
Can you fix this?

more.def: To repair something that is broken or not working.
examples: Dad fixed the leak under the sink.
She fixed the tear in her jacket.
The mechanic fixes cars at the shop.

easy.def: To make food or a drink.
examples: Mom fixes lunch.
I will fix a snack.
Dad fixed dinner.

more.def: To prepare food or a drink.
examples: Dad fixed pancakes for breakfast.
Can I fix you a cup of tea?
She fixed sandwiches for the picnic.
